title: Backend mid systemdesign chat backend
question: Design the backend for a basic one-on-one chat feature: users can send messages in real time and see message history when they open a conversation.
idealAnswer:
Proposes a persistent connection mechanism for real-time delivery, e.g. WebSockets, and explains why plain request/response polling either wastes resources (frequent polling) or adds latency (infrequent polling)

Separates the real-time delivery path from persistence: a message gets written to a database (for history) and also pushed to the recipient's live connection if they're online, rather than the client having to poll storage for new messages

Designs a reasonable data model for message history, e.g. a messages table keyed by conversation id with a timestamp/sequence for ordering, indexed to fetch a conversation's recent messages efficiently

Addresses the offline case: if the recipient isn't connected, the message still needs to be durably stored so it's there when they next open the app, and mentions how the client would know to fetch new messages on reconnect

Considers how a message gets routed to the right connection when the user could be connected to any one of multiple server instances, e.g. a presence/routing layer or pub-sub between instances
